I2.quote: The resulting template-free carbon materials synthesized from MCM-41, IITM-56, SBA-15, MCM-48, SBA-11, and KIT-6 templates were designated as NCCR-41, NCCR-56, CMK-3, CMK-1, NCCR-11, and CMK-8 respectively.
I2.location: main, p. 2 (journal p. 4544), Methodology, Synthesis and Characterization

I3.quote: NCCR-41 shows the highest excess adsorption with an adsorption capacity of 0.29 wt % at 50 bar at room temperature and 2.0 wt % at 77 K and 8 bar pressure.

I5.quote: Ordered mesoporous carbons NCCR-41, NCCR-56, CMK-3, CMK-1, NCCR-11, and CMK-8 with varying pore size and pore dimensionality are prepared by adopting a nanocasting method employing sucrose as a carbon source and various ordered mesoporous silica templates.
I5.location: main, p. 1 (journal p. 4543), Abstract, first sentence

notes: Volumetric (Micromeritics HPVA, Sieverts-type) excess H2 isotherms at 77 K and 298 K up to ~50 bar on six sucrose-derived ordered mesoporous carbons (Figures 9-10). Carbon content 89.1-94.5 wt% C by elemental analysis (Table 2). BET areas 787-1168 m2/g for all six carbons (Table 2); Table 1 BET areas are for the silica templates, not H2 sorbents. Modeling (modified D-A fits, absolute uptake, heats) is in addition to measured data. Ref. 35 (same authors, Catal. Green Chem. Eng. 2018) reports H2 sorption on NCCR-41 and CMK-3, but the paper does not state that its uptake values were published before, so duplicate_data does not apply. record.json is_retracted false; no retraction notice in the PDF.
